column14:
Key Insights
 - The implementation shows mixed progress with solid advancement in sales use cases but significant challenges in service platform deployment, particularly around the customer Service and Living Benefits use cases where the Data Science team's concerns could impact the program's future.
 - Lack of AI Strategy: Pru either doesn’t have an AI strategy or they have not shared it with us
 - Limited business presence - key stakeholders are IT, not business leaders 
 - Leadership Alignment: Fixed income leadership, now overseeing PGIM, will play a key role in deciding the direction of DC and AF use cases. The PGIM (investments management) opportunity is significant, as it involves unifying data and seller experiences across eight previously siloed affiliates. Data Cloud is seen as a crucial component for this unification.
 - Renewal Strategy: Due to a lack of consumption planning, Prudential has an excess of credits. The current one-year renewal will be followed by a longer 3-5 year renewal, where credits will be right-sized. The plan includes migrating to A1 and utilizing flex credits, potentially through external agents, before the next renewal.
 

 Product & Technical Limitations
 - 2 orgs (Life and Fixed Income) have both AF Conversations and Flex Credits as the SELA has Conversations. There is no current plan to fix the contract as this would cause a renegotiation of the SELA. Will address either if Fixed Income or Life choose to pursue an agent prior to the contract renegotiation in July, or when the SELA is renegotiated in July.
 - Annuities Agent isn't consuming credits because Pru hasn't set up their Data Cloud One org. This is a known bug, but no current plan to fix it.
 - Accuracy Issues: A major impediment to wider adoption of Agentforce agents (customer service, co-pilot, live in benefits) is their accuracy. The Living Benefits use case is at 83% accuracy (with a target of 95%), and the Customer Support use case is at 88%.
 - Agent Graph Availability: The Agent Graph, a potential solution for scalability, will not be generally available until Q1 or Q2 of next year, limiting current production capabilities.
 - Authentication Issues: There are ongoing technical challenges related to authentication that need to be resolved.
 - Difficulty Implementing Single Agent Across Orgs: It is currently difficult to implement a single agent use case across Prudential's various Salesforce organizations.
 - Data Science Team Pushback: Continued resistance from Pru's Data Science team trying to convince business leaders that Agentforce isn't the right solution
 

 Customer Implementation Gaps & Delays
 - Configuration and Data Quality: Initial configurations by Prudential did not adhere to best practices. The effectiveness of the agents is highly dependent on the quality of knowledge fed from SharePoint documents, which are often incorrectly formatted, confusing, or contain conflicting information (not Salesforce knowledge).
 - Organizational Hurdles: There's a lack of a technical PM aligned to milestones, too many stakeholders ("cooks in the kitchen"), and a data science team that believes in building their own solutions rather than fully embracing Salesforce.
 - Internal Processes: There's a need to bypass internal business analysis for already built use cases in Omni to speed up deployment.
 - Lack of Technical PM: There is a fundamental lack of a technical Project Manager aligned to customer-agreed milestones, leading to project delays and scope creep.
 - Too Many Stakeholders: The presence of "too many cooks in the kitchen" and a data science team that prefers building its own solutions rather than fully adopting Salesforce contribute to organizational hurdles.
 - Internal Process Bottlenecks: The need to bypass internal business analysis for already developed use cases in Omni is a recognized issue, slowing down deployment.
 - Minimal Agent Usage: Despite being in production, the customer service agent, co-pilot, and live in benefits use cases are used sporadically or for very limited hours per week.
 - Uncertainty in Prioritization: Prudential is unsure how to prioritize Data Cloud, leading to delays in rolling out new initiatives to address attrition.
 - FDE Program Conclusion: The FDE (Field Development Engineer) team, which has dedicated significant time to Prudential, will be concluding its program in January, potentially impacting future support.
 -one AF use case for Customer Service is blocked - Pru doesn't want to move forward with this agent even though it has a greater than 90% accuracy.
 - No plan to consume DC credits outside of AF use cases, even though they do want to consolidate their orgs.

Current Agentforce Use Case(s):
 1. Customer Service Agent: Customer Service Agent deflects external service calls to the Pru Service Center. This agent is in pre-prod, ready to be released in January. However, currently blocked by Pru, despite the FDE team achieving their changing goal posts especially with regards to accuracy. Highest potential consumer of credits at 264M Flex Credits annually. 
 2. SDR agent for Retirement - qualified leads and sets up calls with whole sellers. Set to go live in February 2026, low risk to go to production. Second highest credit volume of the 4 initial metered use cases at an estimated 141M annual flex credits. 
 3. Annuity Withdrawals: After verifying the user, this Custom Agent calculates annuity withdrawals and creates case for user. Est. 15k annual flex credits, set to go live February 2026. Low risk to implementation. 
 4. Living Benefits: After verifying the user, this Custom Agent calculates living benefits and creates case for user. This use case is in pre-production, and will be ready to go live in April 2026, as long as Pru gives the green light. Currently at medium risk to not make it to production. Would consume 2.3M flex credits/year. 
 5. [Unmetered] Co-pilot (Case Summary and Account Summary): This feature has been live for several months and is used sporadically by service agents.
 

 Future Agentforce Use Cases 
 1. Mobile Activity Capture: This is a custom-built co-pilot solution, now an employee agent, that allows sales representatives to capture notes after meetings using voice, which then triggers tasks and opportunities. It's currently being piloted in production and is expected to be fully operational by the end of the year.
 2. Pre-meeting Prep: This employee agent is designed to gather important information for sales personnel before meetings with advisors, and it is also slated for rollout by the end of the year.
 3. Knowledge Agent for Sales Across Affiliates: Agentforce is being considered as a knowledge agent to assist sales teams in cross-selling across different PGIM affiliates. This would include features like activity capture record summaries, post-meeting follow-ups, and pre-meeting preparation, especially as Data Cloud becomes a central repository for meeting prep information.
 

 Current Data Cloud Use Case(s):
 1. Customer Service Agent Knowledge and Audit - All SharePoint content is in DC. Currently in use for the Services organization
 

 Future Data Cloud Use Cases
 1. Unified Profile for Sales/PGIM: mostly across SF orgs (Service, Claims, Annuities, Life) Apr-Oct 2026 Target Date
 2. Sales Agent Knowledge and Audit - All SharePoint content will be in DC

column14:
Key Insights
 - CIO has broad Agentforce strategy, and wants Agentforce for Service deployed across their workforce. Agentforce is a part of their 2026 strategy
 - There's an internal directive not to fully leverage Data Cloud until initial problems are resolved.
 

 Product & Technical Limitations
 1) Lack of transparency in consumption and cost: There's no clear, rock-solid way to see what they are spending or how they are consuming resources, making it difficult to understand costs from beginning to end.
 2) No preview sandboxes for Agent Force: Unlike other product releases where preview sandboxes are available to test new versions and prepare for production, Agent Force does not offer this luxury, leading to unexpected breaks when updates are rolled out.
 3) Custom solutions required: Eugene's IT team had to create a custom solution to pull DLO/DLM data directly into their internal system to pair it with existing data and track service appointment costs.
 4) Unexpected changes breaking scripts: Changes on the backend for the LLM (Large Language Model) caused their scripts for Otto to stop returning the same values, requiring a complete rewrite and consuming a significant portion of their sandbox credits.
 

 Customer Implementation Gaps & Delays
 1) Internal guardrail processes: Storing data or having other systems pull data requires going through an internal process called "guardrails," which involves checks on who is accessing the cloud, what data is being requested, and where it's going, especially concerning potential compromises.

Formerly a brand marketing org, the marketing team is now tasked with transforming towards a growth marketing model. Key Insights
 - Assurant was sold AF and Data 360 at the end of Sept, and Pro Serv kicked off a use case workshop to help with implementation at the end of September.
 - Assurant believes Agentforce will be the differentiator for driving business growth and efficiency. Data 360 primarily being used to fuel data for agents so far (unified data layer for Multiple Experience portals, cross-org data harmonization for agent-to-agent
 communication, and knowledge base centralization supporting multiple agents)
 - The Data Cloud implementation is foundational to their Agentforce success, serving as the data backbone that enables intelligent, contextual agent interactions across their home warranty ecosystem
 

 

 Product & Technical Limitations
 - Service Agent blocker: Custom Lightning Web Components (LWC) are NOT supported on Service Agent for external customers on portals. Custom LWC components are only available for Employee Agents, not Service Agents. This affects their ability to create custom input/output components for their external-facing portal. No clear workaround available - they need specific guidance on how to handle this limitation
 - Platform Infrastructure Issues: Agentforce provisioning failures due to Data Cloud mapping changes after EGL (Extended Go-Live). Risk of customers ending up in "cross FI" situations. Changes made after EGL of Data Cloud, AI Platform, and UMA without proper notification to other clouds
 - Customer "really unhappy" due to: Errors in data libraries, Failures in Data Cloud connections, Any changes in Agentforce create setup errors where it's not fetching the data library
 - Architecture issues: 
 1) Separate org architecture creates complexity - they want agent-to-agent communication between Experience Cloud portals in different orgs
 2) Palantir to Agentforce migration concerns - they currently have Palantir agents but want to explore Agentforce replacement
 3) Knowledge article management becomes complicated with separate sets for different portals and agent
 

 Customer Implementation Gaps & Delays
 - No ETA on LWC support for ASA (Agentforce Service Agent) embedded in non-SF Experience sites
 - Custom Lightning Types & Renditions are available for Agentforce (Default) and Employee Agent but NOT for ASA
 - Questions raised about whether current assigned resources are sufficient for this strategic implementation

Lowe's is using Data Cloud with a focus on optimizing data cloud credit consumption. Key aspects of their usage and related discussions include:
 

  * **Credit Consumption Management:** The IT department is highly focused on ensuring every credit is used without running out, as they have a billion credits remaining until July 2026.
  * **Ingestion vs. Activation:** They are clarifying that "ingestion" (Marketing Cloud to Data Cloud) is zero credits, while "activation" (Data Cloud to Marketing Cloud) consumes credits.
  * **Tableau Integration:** There's an inquiry into how Tableau impacts Data Cloud credits, and Kevin Mathew Galang is investigating this.
  * **Marketing Cloud Connection:** The connection between Marketing Cloud (MCE) and Data Cloud (DC) is established by enabling Marketing Cloud as a source in Data Cloud using credentials, not a separate connector product.
  * **Marketing Campaign Analytics:** Marketing campaign analytics is not considered a good use for Data Cloud due to a lack of out-of-the-box reporting, with Tableau or marketing intelligence suggested as alternatives.
  * **Advanced Capabilities with MCA:** Adding the Marketing Cloud Advanced (MCA) SKU will unlock cross-journey orchestration, marketing performance and campaign dashboards, and agentic journey decisioning, but not the digital wallet.
  * **Segmentation Credit Consumption:** There's a question about whether previewing segment counts before publishing consumes credits, which Kevin Mathew Galang is also investigating due to conflicting information.
  * **Customer Education:** Kevin Mathew Galang is preparing a presentation deck to address customer questions on consumption and estimate credit usage, emphasizing the importance of backing up claims with public documentation.  - They will want to import the knowledge base in Data Cloud along with Claims and Policy data to fuel future Agentic use cases.
 

 Product & Technical Limitations
 - Currently on Conversations SKU which doesn't allow for the Employee Agent OOTB features. Currently working to switch them to a Agentforce Foundations SKU which will enable 5 OOTB agents at zero cost. Eventually will want to transfer them to an A4X SKU, but they don't need additional OOTB features/functionalities at this point.
 - - High latency for the account table [GUS records: W-19275054,W-19308744; Case Number: 471128155]
 - CDC Capability in Data Cloud - Zero Copy only works by Query, but AmFam wants the Zero Copy connector to work as a push so that Data Cloud pushes the data to GCP as soon as it's created. Workaround in place using platform events
 - Shared datasets were linked via BigQuery Omni (Data Cloud), originating from aws-us-east-1. To make the data available in GCP’s BigQuery Multi-Region (e.g., us), we had to create multiple Materialized Views (MVs)—both local and multi-region
 - Sev 1 Case 471800834- Data Stream Refresh Failure - Insurance Object (and other objects) were not Refreshed
 - Sev 1 Case - Alias Issue (Case # 471732151) Copado Pipeline failed from QA2 to Prod (Environment deployment). As customers try to deploy Data Kits through Copado pipelines, there are failures due to unwanted inactive connections are being created with different org IDs. column16: Fortinet has made significant progress, with their first Agent Force MVP use case going live on June 6. While Professional Services assisted with the initial setup, their engagement is concluding soon, and Fortinet expresses confidence in their internal capabilities to manage Agent Force going forward, preferring self-reliance over extended ProServe engagement. It's important to note that Fortinet has separate teams managing Agent Force and Data Cloud, though both report to the same IT department. Joseph, the consumption seller, covers both Agent Force and Data Cloud accounts and actively project manages their implementation and health post-sales. He is also the point of contact for gathering more details from Carmen Lazoya, the ProServe contact for Agent Force. column14: Fortinet uses Data Cloud to improve lead management and data usage, primarily for Global BDR Lead Scoring, which allows for more complex and accurate scoring than their previous system by running separate scores for leads and contacts. They also aim to report website metrics via a direct SDK integration to Tableau, use website data for segmentation to convert unknown visitors into known ones, and aggregate intent data from various providers to push to Salesforce for sales team visibility. Additionally, Data Cloud is used for data enrichment programs (e.g., normalizing data, deriving job functions), and a separate team is exploring prediction modeling. Their data sources include leads, contacts, Salesforce data, Google Ads, SFTP (for transactional data, Eloqua, Adobe Analytics), and various intent data providers, with a Mulesoft integration replacing Eloqua's direct connection. A key aspect is their ability to change records through the transform process, which differentiates their use case from Customer Insights.
column15:
Fortinet faced significant challenges, primarily related to Data Cloud's consumption and implementation. A major issue was incorrect credit sizing upon switching from CDP, leading to rapid consumption of 250k credits within about eight days, causing concern for the CMO. This was exacerbated by suboptimal data ingestion practices, such as pumping excessive rows and ingesting all historical web data (14 years of Adobe data) without initial filtering. They also struggled with segmentation activation due to the high volume of leads needing near real-time updates and found the website SDK integration "totally stuck" as Salesforce support indicated it required professional services or developer involvement rather than just troubleshooting. Other issues included a lack of visibility into consumption dashboards for several weeks post-go-live, Data Cloud's slower resolution time compared to Eloqua, problems with a new Google Analytics connector, difficulty keeping up with rapid product changes, and access blocked issues for Salesforce documentation.
 

 Despite initial challenges, Fortinet has made significant progress and is in a much better position, with 80-90% of their initial problems resolved. The critical credit consumption issue was corrected by re-sizing their allocation and providing a one-time $0 order form to cover consumed credits. They significantly improved web data ingestion by reducing history to 30 days and optimized transform processes, leading to much lower consumption. As a result, the initially "angry" customer is now a "fan," satisfied with the fixes and actively seeking further assistance. They are seeing clear value in Data Cloud, recognizing its superiority over Eloqua for complex lead scoring, and the account is considered to have strong growth potential with new use cases identified. Fortinet is excited to use a sandbox environment to prevent future issues, indicating they are "very far along" in their Data Cloud journey and in a "very healthy spot" with most existing data connections pushing data successfully.
column16: The initial engagement focused on optimization to resolve existing issues rather than identifying new use cases. Fortinet's team communicates primarily via Teams, with email preferred for issue reporting, though Slack is an option. Internal tracking is maintained through a "consumption plan" document, updated weekly and shared with the account team. It's important to note that Salesforce support handles troubleshooting but not implementation for complex issues like the SDK integration, which requires professional services or internal development resources.

1. Agent Access Use Case (Proof of Concept/POC)
 This use case is currently agreed upon as a Proof of Concept (POC) and is considered one of the fastest moving use cases, located in the Schedule Hub org.
 • Problem: Agents currently lack sufficient training when attempting to reschedule appointments. They often rely on a system called Pendo for guidance but sometimes must raise a ticket in ServiceNow because they do not know how to proceed.
 • Goal/Solution: The objective is to provide step-by-step guidance sourced from a Knowledge Base (KB). The project focuses heavily on Enablement and Adoption, requiring a dedicated team for Adoption & Change Management for Agentforce.
 2. No Shows (Next Priority)
 This use case addresses missed appointments and their associated consequences.
 • Problem: Abandoned appointment slots are currently not followed up on.
 • Current Process: Non-clinical teams are responsible for identifying missed appointments. They then work with SAs (Scheduling Assistants) to reschedule these missed appointments. The process involves phone calls that are manual and not standardized.
 • Goal/Solution: The aim is to automate reschedules and send reminders. Relatedly, there was discussion about an automated way for a patient to send a message about missing/late appointments prior to the scheduled time.
 • Data Source: Knowing when a patient missed an appointment relies on data from an External System EHR, which is a homegrown solution called CWOW.
 • Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Revenue Loss and Customer Satisfaction.
 3. Late Appointments (Following Priority)
 This use case focuses on the disruptive effects of patient punctuality.
 • Problem: Patients who show up late for appointments cause a knock-on effect across the clinic schedule.
 • Goal: DaVita aims to determine how to effectively address these issues.
 Other Contextual Details
 The team discussed related aspects for these use cases, including the use of text message reminders and confirmation, though caution was raised about not overwhelming patients who require three treatments per week. The Product Owner, Lance, has been involved in discussions with Business Stakeholders, and next steps include Discovery Sessions where the team plans to be included in interviews with clinic staff to understand operations.
 The fact that the fastest moving use cases, including the paid POC, are in the Schedule Hub org (which only has 5,000 conversations allocated) presented a critical challenge, as the majority of conversations (nearly 700,000) are allocated to the P3 org, which has the slowest moving Agent Force use cases. This discrepancy was identified as the potential primary revenue-driving event.

#Overview#
 I am currently supporting the AE in unlocking the resale of Agentforce and clearly demonstrating its value. On October 24th, the customer migrated their summarization solution to their own LLM, which significantly reduced their ER credit consumption. As a result, ER overage is no longer a concern, and they decided to postpone the renewal to Flex Credits.
 After returning from vacation, I reconnected with the account team, who shared a new direction for the account strategy. The AE met with the MRV CEO, who is now open to evaluating a solution that helps qualify the leads that will come from the Big Brother Brasil reality show (which MRV will sponsor).
 This brings a new challenge: we must quickly deliver a solution that is high-value and high-impact, so the customer can finally see the tangible benefits of Agentforce. Up to this point, they haven’t fully recognized its value; they mainly perceive that several teams are involved in the initiative, but without meaningful outcomes.
 On the other hand, the customer agreed to run a workshop, but they requested a more technical one, aimed at spreading Agentforce knowledge among MRV’s technical team (since this expertise currently sits mostly with the IS partner’s staff working on-site).
 My plan is to be present on that day and use the opportunity to provide them with a valuable, concrete explanation of Agentforce and its capabilities.
 

 #Nexts Steps#
 Final week of November: 
 1. Follow up with the Account Team regarding the rapid-turnaround initiative for the Big Brother project.
 2. Confirm workshop date: Secure the workshop date so I can attend in person.

column16:
October final notes: I connected with the customer during Dreamforce and introduced them to Bessa. I also met with their IS Partner. The customer shared that they had developed a summarization solution using their own LLM, which is about to be deployed. As a result ER (now and the Flex Credits in the future) consumption is expected to decrease significantly. They just received a curtesy of ER to avoid their overage. They were almost at 100% of their usage of ER. Now they are on 77% of consumption. 
 The customer is currently in the final stages of migrating to Agentforce for Sales SKU. Regarding Data Cloud, they expressed interest in deepening their understanding of the platform. They currently have two Data Cloud licenses, one originally sold for Marketing purposes and another bundled with Agentforce, though the customer is not fully aware of this distinction.
 Past Context: This customer was referred by the AEs to receive guidance on best practices for credit consumption and to address project issues related to Agentforce Analytics data.
 After the initial engagement, which covered Agentforce Analytics enablement, Data Cloud implications, and OOTB reporting, the customer reported a new issue: high Einstein Request (ER) consumption. With the Consumption Lead investigation, we identified that the usage originated from a summarization prompt deployed in Experience Cloud, considering an external agent. An internal investigation was initiated, and both Salesforce and the customer opened tickets to analyze the case.
 Due to limited access to the org and partner restrictions, troubleshooting took additional time. Eventually, it was confirmed that the ER volume was aligned with actual usage, with no product defect or duplicated requests detected.
 #Next Steps#
 On October 20th, I met with the Core AE, and we aligned on the following next steps:
 1. Hold a meeting with the customer to review credit consumption and the transition from Conversations to Flex Credits, providing enablement on credit management within the Agentforce for Sales SKU - Scheduled on Thursday 23rd. 
 2. Propose on the Thursday call an Agentforce Use Case Workshop to identify and unblock new opportunities for credit utilization, since their current summarization use case will no longer run inside Salesforce.
 3. Reposition Data Cloud to drive adoption and ensure the customer begins using its full capabilities effectively.
 Oct 7th: The customer is expected to attend Dreamforce (AE to confirm travel plans), where I plan to connect with them in person. We are currently awaiting the commercial transition to Flex Credits to design a headless Agentforce solution that would convert their current ER usage into Flex Credits, serving as a temporary approach until they are ready to migrate to A4X/A1.

 Phase 1 – Initial conversation with the implementation partner to understand the current Agentforce setup and existing issues.
 Phase 2 – Meeting with the customer to cover topics such as Credit Consumption, Digital Wallet, Agentforce Analytics, Generative AI and Feedback, and OOTB Dashboards and Reports.

 Phase 5 – Optimize and enhance existing use cases and identify opportunities to expand Agentforce use cases.

 Customer meeting summary:
 Amy Dolk sent a recap to Matthew Poirier regarding the Data Cloud consumption levers and cost implications for evaluating Salesforce Loyalty Management (SFLM) versus Eagle Eye for Sally Beauty (SBH).
 The primary takeaway is that native Salesforce-to-Salesforce integration, such as SFLM, offers a "zero-cost" ingestion advantage, unlike external sources like Eagle Eye, which incur a credit cost of 2,000 credits per 1 million rows for batch ingestion or 5,000 credits per 1 million rows for streaming ingestion.
 A critical cost differentiator is Profile Unification (Identity Resolution), where adding an external source like Eagle Eye would typically require a full IDR refresh consuming an estimated 5.6 million credits for 56 million total rows, while SFLM's native integration may not trigger a full refresh, offering significant potential savings.
 The volume estimates being modeled for Sally Beauty are ~44 million Loyalty Profile Records and ~346 million Loyalty Engagement Data records brought in daily.

column16:

When these credits are filtered out, more specific Data Cloud consumption details emerge, showing credit usage across categories like batch data pipelines and batch data transforms. A key consideration is the fixed daily consumption for Data Cloud, which persists even if conversations are paused.
 

 Salesforce itself is the implementation partner for Data Cloud at Lennar. Challenge 
 

 reMarkable's contact center team of 300+ agents across Serbia, Norway, and Philippines faces significant operational challenges:
 Fragmented Customer Experience: Customers contact support multiple times over multiple days, creating disconnected experiences with no visibility into conversation history
 Low AI Deflection: Current Mark service agent handles only 25,000 of 225,000 monthly chat conversations (11% deflection), well below the industry benchmark of 50%
 Agent Productivity Gaps: Contact center agents manually search SOPs and knowledge bases without AI-powered recommendations, leading to inconsistent service quality and longer handle times
 Swivel Chair Problem: Agents work across multiple systems (Salesforce, DHL, carrier apps) without unified data access, impacting efficiency
 Minimal Credit Utilization: Despite having 214M Flex Credits allocated, reMarkable currently uses only 3%, indicating untapped potential for AI-powered automation
 With customer satisfaction (CSAT), Net Promoter Score (NPS), and case handle time as key metrics, reMarkable needs to scale their Agentforce capabilities to improve both customer and employee experiences.
 

 Desired Outcomes
 For Customers (External - Mark Agent):
 Achieve 50% deflection rate by December 2025 (currently at 11%)
 Increase post-chat survey score to 70% from current baseline
 Reduce new customer escalation rate from 40% to under 20% within first 30 days
 Provide 24/7 intelligent support with context-aware troubleshooting across device setup, sync issues, order tracking, and account management
 Enable proactive issue detection for known firmware and hardware problems
 For Agents (Internal - Employee Agent):
 Improve agent productivity through AI-powered knowledge recommendations and writing assistance
 Reduce average handle time by 35% for common technical issues
 Increase first-contact resolution rates to 60%+ through better case context and recommendations
 Enhance employee satisfaction by eliminating repetitive manual tasks
 Provide transparent case lifecycle visibility across customer touchpoints
 Business Impact:
 Improve overall CSAT and NPS scores
 Reduce support costs through intelligent deflection
 Decrease product return rates by improving first-30-day customer experience
 Demonstrate strong credit utilization (from 3% to 230% of allocation)

#Challenge#
 The customer recently renewed their CDP license; however, the AE is seeking to transition them to Data Cloud as soon as possible to unblock additional initiatives. I have been working closely with both the AE and the IS Partner through a dedicated WhatsApp group to coordinate next steps and ensure alignment. Segmentation has been identified as one of the main drivers of elevated credit consumption.
 Prior to Dreamforce, the implementation partner and the Salesforce team, including myself, conducted an analysis of the existing segment data. We identified several segments with duplicated filters and consolidated them into Calculated Insights. Although the experiment resulted in only a minor change in the total number of rows, the overall impact on consumption was limited.
 On October 7th, I held a follow-up meeting with the IS partner to review the largest DMOs and explore optimization opportunities. During this session, we identified a DMO containing approximately 9 billion rows, used across multiple segmentations as an exclusion filter. By restructuring this into a nested segment that runs once per day and feeds the primary pilot segment, we successfully reduced the number of processed rows from 12.4 billion to 941 million, achieving a 92.3% reduction.
 Additionally, I noted that several segments are currently scheduled and activated continuously, including weekends. I recommended adjusting the schedule to weekdays only, as this capability was not previously available in CDP/Data Cloud.
 

 #Next Steps#
 1. The IS Partner will replicate the optimized nested segment across all segmentations leveraging the “Email Engagement” DMO to measure the overall impact. Expect to gather some results in Superset by the end of this week (by Oct 24th)/ 2. Monitor and validate the implementation of updated scheduling to restrict activation to weekdays.

AF USE CASE(s):
 Based on the Statement of Work (SOW) overview provided, here are the top 5 use cases 
 

 These use cases are designed to unify data across systems (Salesforce, JIRA, Slack, GAM, DCM) to power AI-driven agents that assist internal teams with case management, customer insights, and campaign performance.
 

 ----------------------------------
 1. Holistic Case Triage and Resolution (Internal Agent)This use case empowers support agents to resolve cases faster by using AI to instantly analyze historical data across multiple platforms.
 

 How it works: An internal Agentforce agent analyzes a specific case number and searches for similar historical Cases, JIRA tickets, Knowledge Articles, and Slack messages.
 

 The Goal: The agent suggests triage steps and resolution guidance based on what has worked in the past, reducing research time and ensuring consistent support.
 ----------------------------------
 

 2. Campaign Performance "Traffic Light" Signals (Internal Agent)This use case provides Campaign Managers with real-time, AI-driven insights into how their campaigns are performing without needing to run complex reports.
 

 How it works: Data Cloud ingests and harmonizes 1st and 3rd party data (from GAM, DCM, etc.) and compares it against Salesforce benchmarks. It calculates a "Traffic Light" status (Red, Yellow, Green) for each campaign.
 

 The Goal: An Agentforce agent can answer questions like "Why is this campaign Red?" and provide playbook instructions on mitigation steps to get the campaign back on track.
 ----------------------------------
 

 3. Customer History Analysis with RecommendationsThis use case allows agents to instantly understand a customer's entire relationship and status without clicking through multiple tabs or systems.
 

 How it works: An Agentforce agent reviews general account data, open case history, open JIRA tickets, recent email summaries, and active services. The agent can answer prompts like "What's going on with this customer?" or "What should I do next?".
 

 The Goal: To intelligently surface insights and recommend proactive next steps (e.g., offering a specific resolution based on history).
 ----------------------------------
 

 4. Deep Search for FAQs & KnowledgeThis splits the search functionality into "Quick" and "Deep" modes to give agents the right level of detail for the problem at hand.
 

 How it works:
  Quick Search: primarily searches CRM data and Knowledge for fast answers.
  Deep Search: extends the search into external data via Data Cloud, including Slack messages, JIRA issues/comments, and Confluence pages.
 

 The Goal: To allow agents to uncover broader context from external sources when complex issues arise, while keeping simple queries fast.
 ----------------------------------
 

 5. Automated Case Action PlansThis use case automates the administrative side of case management by having the AI suggest operational tasks.
 

 How it works:Based on the current case activity and similar historical cases, the Agentforce agent suggests a specific "Case Action Plan."
 

 The Goal: To proactively identify follow-up actions such as scheduling a meeting, setting a reminder, sending an email, or recommending an escalation, ensuring no steps are missed in the workflow.
 ----------------------------------
 

 Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1rmP74_0KAdPAMcX1F1y8mz6rz4pqe05nhcFX4kKjCO0/edit?slide=id.g38bbbeba8da_0_138#slide=id.g38bbbeba8da_0_138

#Overview#
 The customer had previously implemented an Agentforce use case, though with limited adoption, and the agent is currently inactive. Following the recent renewal of their Conversations entitlements, they have expressed openness to developing a new Agentforce proof of concept (POC).
 #Current State# - Guiding them after the Use Case Workshop
 On November 19th, the day I returned from vacation, I had a call with the team to review some automation initiatives that other Unimed teams had mapped and that could potentially be transformed into Agentforce actions. I made it clear that we need to stay focused, avoid duplicating efforts, and not deviate from the use case we previously prioritized.
 

 Earlier that same day, November 19th, the Account AE scheduled time with me to discuss the account strategy. The RVP’s intention is to drive some credit sales in Q4, which means we need to build a solid Consumption Plan and estimate future usage across all use cases. I am on it! This is especially challenging since they haven’t started consuming anything yet.
 

 On October 24th, we held the Use Case Readout session, where we presented the roadmap plan and provided them with a detailed template as homework to formalize the first Agentforce use case (including KPIs, data sources, deployment location, challenges, and more). This deliverable is still pending on their side. I followed up again when I returned from vacation, and they said they would get back to us on November 28th.
 #Nexts Steps# 
  - Nov 28th: meeting with Everymind directors to push a plan for their side. (done)
 - Week of Dec 2nd - Align the storytelling about the Consumption Plan to be present to Unimed Stakeholders (Rodrigo Cuello is in São Paulo and we are trying to talk to him about the account and strategy) 
 - Weekly Cadence every Monday (on going)

From original PWC Implementation Notes:
 Salesforce Data Cloud Implementation Outline
 1. Objective
 Centralize patient data to enable a unified 360-degree view.
 Enhance segmentation, activation, and personalization in Marketing Cloud.
 Optimize Health Cloud storage by offloading high-volume data (e.g., Encounters, Appointments).
 2. Integration Points
 Epic
 Real-time ingestion via MuleSoft Ingestion API (Encounter, Appointment, Preference, and Patient Attribute data).
 Monthly batch SFTP feeds for additional segmentation data.
 Salesforce Health Cloud
 Native connector to share account/contact records and support data re-ingestion for deleted records.
 Wrapper classes and anonymous Apex used to extract deleted records for re-upload via MuleSoft.
 Salesforce Marketing Cloud
 Preference data ingested and mapped to support compliance and targeting.
 Used for journey activation (e.g., lung and breast screening campaigns).
 Salesforce CRM
 Contact and Account data streamed via native connectors.
 Forms the foundation for unified profiles through Data Cloud identity resolution.
 3. Data Cloud Configuration
 Identity Resolution
 Primary Data Model Object: Individual
 Matching based on MRN using Party Identification object.
 Rulesets configured for match and reconciliation logic.
 Unified Profiles
 Consolidates patient data from all sources into a single profile.
 Enables downstream use in segmentation, insights, and personalization.
 Unified Contact Points & Links
 Retains all valid addresses, phones, and emails.
 Tracks source-to-unified profile relationships.
 4. Data Model & Object Mapping
 Custom and standard DMOs created to model:
 Appointments
 Encounters
 Communication Subscription Consent
 Marketing Cloud Preferences
 Epic Problem Lists and Attributes
 Relationships defined between core objects: Account, Account Contact, Individual, Party Identification, etc.
 5. Data Streams & Permissions
 Data streams defined per source (CRM, Epic, SFTP).
 Configured using appropriate field-level security via Permission Sets.
 Validated against Mapping Spec documentation.
 6. Deleted Records Management
 Quarterly deletion in Health Cloud triggers mirrored deletions in Data Cloud.
 Custom Apex tools extract deleted records.
 Manual validation to exclude Marketing Cloud journey participants.
 Final datasets re-ingested to Data Cloud via MuleSoft-formatted CSVs.

The customer is testing several agents in Sandbox and noticed Einstein Requests (ER) consumption in scenarios where they believed ER wouldn’t be used. However, we later discovered that the actual source was another use case leveraging Agentforce. Through a video request about the agent, we confirmed they were using Agentforce Default, which continues to consume ER even under Flex Credits. The use case is an agent that answers employee questions about Cases and Opportunities.

Additionally, they would like to use the Data Cloud One in certain orgs, which is not currently possible due to the way the SKUs were provisioned. Absa is a strategic account within the EGM region and a customer of both Data Cloud and Agentforce.
 

 One of the main challenges at Absa is their highly siloed structure - multiple departments operate independently, with limited cross-team communication. The organization has a complex operating model and a general lack of clear ownership over initiatives, which creates fragmentation and slows progress.
 

 They have implemented an Agentforce use case (FAQ Agent) and are currently in discussions with the account team to explore and position additional ones. On the Data Cloud side, they have some use cases (Marketing Activation) already in production. 
 Currently, they are in the renewal phase, which presents an important opportunity to reposition the value of both platforms. The account team is actively working to introduce and estimate new Data Cloud and Agentforce use cases, aiming to regain momentum and deliver clear business value.
 

 A significant spike in usage a few months ago led to a temporary loss of trust in Salesforce, so careful alignment and clear planning will be key to re-establishing confidence and securing long-term engagement.

column14:
Key Insights 
 - Currently, Guardian uses DC at a CDP for their Dental Providers. 
 - They also have Segment which is their "true" CDP for the company, and they historically have not wanted to replace it or expand much on their DC usage. More recently, they've been open to replacing it, so we are beginning to have conversations here. 
 - Scoping and exploring 3 different Agentforce use cases. We have an order form out for flex credits to support the first one (SDR agent). 
 - Additionally, they are looking into Tableau Next and want to better understand how DC can help with pulling data in for Tableau. 
 - Pardot replacement with DC and MCE 
 

 Product & Technical Limitations 
 

 Customer Implementation Delays and Gaps
column15:
Current Use Case: 
 1) Traditional CDP use case for their Dental Providers. Cross-Channel Data Integration by connecting Marketing Cloud Engagement (MCE) data with other enterprise systems 
 2) Marketing Campaign Segmentation - Using Data Cloud segments to drive Marketing Cloud journeys
 

 Future Use Cases: 
 1) Replacing Segment to bring more functionality into DC. 
 2) Agentforce Integration - Guardian is now also exploring Agentforce pilots alongside their Data Cloud expansion. Post-pilot, plan is to expand to a enterprise-level implementation 
 3) Enhanced Analytics - Considering Tableau integration for more sophisticated reporting and analytics
